grades.reason: Discusses xv6 buffer cache, logging and file-system layout. It has nothing to do with satp or address-translation synchronization.

grades.quote: Note that writing `satp` does not imply any ordering constraints between page-table updates and subsequent address translations, nor does it imply any invalidation of address-translation caches. If the new address space’s page tables have been modified, or if an ASID is reused, it may be necessary to execute an SFENCE.VMA instruction (see Section 12.2.1) after, or in some cases before, writing `satp` .
grades.reason: States that writing satp does not order page-table updates or invalidate address-translation caches. It says SFENCE.VMA may be needed after, or sometimes before, writing satp. This directly answers why an old mapping can still be visible and what synchronization is required.

grades.quote: SFENCE.VMA is also used to invalidate entries in the address-translation cache associated with a hart (see Section 12.3.2).
grades.reason: Describes SFENCE.VMA, the instruction that orders page-table updates and invalidates address-translation cache entries. It also explains the rs1/rs2 variants and that other harts need a separate shootdown. It does not tie the instruction to writing satp, so it is only a partial answer.

grades.quote:
The RISC-V has an instruction sfence.vma that flushes the current CPU’s TLB. Xv6 executes sfence.vma in kvminithart after reloading the satp register, and in the trampoline code for uservec and userret.

It is also necessary to issue sfence.vma before changing satp, in order to wait for completion of all outstanding loads and stores.
grades.reason: Explains that RISC-V TLB entries can go stale after a satp change, so sfence.vma must run after reloading satp. It also says sfence.vma is needed before changing satp, to complete outstanding loads and stores and keep earlier accesses on the old page table.
